question: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948 mainly categorised the large-scale industries into ______ fragments.
solution_text:
The correct answer is four.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR), 1948 was the first industrial policy of independent India, announced by the government on 6 April 1948. (औद्योगिक नीति संकल्प 1948 — चार वर्ग)

 

• It classified large-scale industries into four broad categories based on the degree of state involvement.

 

• Category 1 covered strategic industries reserved exclusively for the State (Central Government) monopoly — arms and ammunition, atomic energy, and railways.

 

• Category 2 covered industries where the State would progressively set up new undertakings, while existing private units could continue and expand — coal, iron and steel, aircraft manufacture, shipbuilding, telephone/telegraph equipment, and mineral oils.

 

• Category 3 covered industries of basic importance where the State would regulate through planning, leaving the rest to private enterprise subject to periodic review; Category 4 covered all remaining industries left to the private sector, subject to general government control.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IPR, 1948 also envisaged the setting up of the Cottage and Small-Scale Industries Board and reaffirmed the importance of cottage and small-scale industries.

 

• It was later replaced by the more detailed Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, which introduced the famous three-fold classification (Schedule A, B, C).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (three/two/five): These do not match the actual four-fold classification laid out in the IPR, 1948.

question:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT vis-à-vis features of the Indian Constitution?

1) The Constitution empowers the Prime Minister to proclaim three types of emergencies.

2) A reservation policy is there to uplift the disadvantaged sections of society.

3) The Supreme Court has no power of judicial review.

4) The Constitution provides for universal adult suffrage.

Which of the above statements are incorrect?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements 1 and 3 are incorrect, while statements 2 and 4 are correct features of the Indian Constitution. (राष्ट्रपति की आपातकालीन शक्तियाँ — न्यायिक पुनरावलोकन)

 

• Statement 1 is incorrect: It is the President of India, not the Prime Minister, who is empowered under the Constitution to proclaim three types of emergency — National Emergency (Article 352), President's Rule/State Emergency (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360).

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: The Supreme Court does possess the power of judicial review, i.e., the power to examine the constitutional validity of legislative enactments and executive orders, derived mainly from Articles 13 and 32.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The Constitution provides for a reservation policy (Articles 15(4), 16(4), etc.) to uplift SCs, STs, and other disadvantaged sections.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: The Constitution provides for universal adult suffrage (Article 326), granting every citizen aged 18 and above the right to vote.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Judicial review in India is narrower than in the USA — it is based on the doctrine of "procedure established by law" rather than "due process of law".

 

• A National Emergency has been proclaimed three times in India so far — 1962, 1971, and 1975.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (2 and 4): Incorrect, since statements 2 and 4 are actually correct, not incorrect.

 

• Option 3 (1 and 2): Incorrect, since statement 2 is a correct statement, not an incorrect one.

 

• Option 4 (3 and 4): Incorrect, since statement 4 is a correct statement, not an incorrect one.

question: Who is the only Indian woman who has been ranked world's no.1 for badminton?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saina Nehwal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saina Nehwal became the first and only Indian woman to be ranked World No. 1 in the BWF women's singles badminton rankings, achieving this feat on 1 April 2015. (साइना नेहवाल — विश्व नंबर 1 बैडमिंटन)

 

• She held the top spot for several weeks in 2015, becoming a landmark achievement for Indian badminton.

 

• Saina Nehwal is also an Olympic bronze medallist (London 2012), a World Championship medallist, and has won the Padma Bhushan (2016), Padma Shri (2010), Arjuna Award (2009) and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2010).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• P.V. Sindhu is a two-time Olympic medallist (Rio 2016 silver, Tokyo 2020 bronze) and a World Champion (2019), but she has not been ranked World No. 1.

 

• Jwala Gutta is a renowned Indian doubles specialist, an Arjuna and Padma Shri awardee.

 

NOTE

 

• P V Sindhu (Option 1): Highly decorated but never attained the World No. 1 singles ranking.

 

• Rituparna Das (Option 2): An Indian badminton player, but not ranked World No. 1.

 

• Jwala Gutta (Option 3): A celebrated doubles player, not a singles World No. 1.

question: Which famous book was written by 'Haripala'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeeta Sudhakara.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sangeeta Sudhakara is a treatise on Indian classical music composed by Haripaladeva (Haripala), a scholar-king associated with medieval musicology. (संगीत सुधाकर — हरिपाल)

 

• The text deals with the theory of raga, tala, and musical composition and is regarded as one of the important pre-Sangeeta Ratnakara musicological works.

 

• It forms part of the broader tradition of Sanskrit musicological literature that shaped classical Hindustani and Carnatic music theory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sangeet Ratnakara, by Sharangadeva (13th century CE), is the most authoritative and comprehensive medieval treatise on Indian music, dance and drama.

 

• Sangeet Darpan was written by Damodara Mishra, while Gita Govinda is a 12th-century Sanskrit lyrical poem by Jayadeva on the love of Radha and Krishna.

 

NOTE

 

• Sangeet Darpan (Option 2): Authored by Damodara Mishra, not Haripala.

 

• Sangeet Ratnakara (Option 3): Authored by Sharangadeva, the most celebrated musicological text of medieval India.

 

• Gita Govinda (Option 4): Authored by the poet Jayadeva, unrelated to Haripala.

question: Which of the following is an example of a 'solid in a liquid' type of solution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tincture of iodine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tincture of iodine is a solution of solid iodine dissolved in liquid alcohol (ethanol), making it a classic example of a solid-in-liquid solution. (आयोडीन टिंचर — ठोस का द्रव में विलयन)

 

• A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances; the substance present in a larger amount is the solvent, and the one in a smaller amount is the solute.

 

• In tincture of iodine, iodine (a solid) is the solute and alcohol (a liquid) is the solvent, giving a solid-in-liquid type solution — commonly used as an antiseptic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vinegar is a liquid-in-liquid solution — acetic acid (liquid) dissolved in water (liquid).

 

• Brass (copper + zinc) and Bronze (copper + tin) are solid-in-solid solutions, commonly called alloys.

 

NOTE

 

• Vinegar (Option 2): A liquid-liquid solution (acetic acid in water), not solid-in-liquid.

 

• Brass (Option 3): A solid-solid alloy of copper and zinc.

 

• Bronze (Option 4): A solid-solid alloy of copper and tin.

question: In September 2022 the book 'Ambedkar and Modi: Reformer's Ideas Performer's Implementation' has been written by which of the following personalities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ram Nath Kovind.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The book 'Ambedkar and Modi: Reformer's Ideas Performer's Implementation' was authored (and launched) by former President of India Ram Nath Kovind in September 2022. (राम नाथ कोविंद — अंबेडकर एंड मोदी पुस्तक)

 

• The book compares the socio-political ideas of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar with the implementation of welfare schemes under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

 

• Ram Nath Kovind served as the 14th President of India (2017-2022) before authoring/launching this work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 refer to other former Presidents of India — Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (2nd President), Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (11th President), and Smt. Pratibha Patil (12th President, and India's first woman President) — none of whom authored this particular book.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (Option 1): India's 2nd President and eminent philosopher; not the author of this book.

 

• APJ Abdul Kalam (Option 2): India's 11th President, known as the "Missile Man"; not the author of this book.

 

• Pratibha Patil (Option 4): India's 12th President and first woman President; not the author of this book.

question: According to Census of India 2011, how many districts are there in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 640.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, the country was divided into 640 districts. (जनगणना 2011 — 640 जिले)

 

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India (7th after independence), conducted with the theme "Our Census, Our Future".

 

• As per Census 2011, India comprised 35 states/UTs, 640 districts, 5,924 sub-districts, 7,935 towns and about 6,40,867 villages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, India's total population was about 121.09 crore, with a decadal growth rate of 17.7% and a sex ratio of 943 females per 1000 males.

 

• The number of districts in India has since increased with the creation of new states/districts (e.g., after the bifurcation creating Telangana in 2014), and now exceeds 640.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (620/630/610): None of these match the actual Census 2011 figure of 640 districts.

question: Mahabalipuram temple was built under the reign of which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pallava.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The monuments and temples of Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), Tamil Nadu, were built by the Pallava dynasty, mainly under Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) and Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha). (महाबलीपुरम मंदिर — पल्लव वंश)

 

• The site is famous for its rathas (monolithic rock-cut temples), the Shore Temple, and the giant open-air relief "Descent of the Ganges" (Arjuna's Penance).

 

• Mahabalipuram was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984 under the name "Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pallavas ruled parts of South India (with capital at Kanchipuram) between the 3rd and 9th centuries CE and were great patrons of Dravidian architecture.

 

• The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram is one of the oldest structural (as opposed to rock-cut) stone temples in South India.

 

NOTE

 

• Rashtrakuta (Option 1): Known for the Kailasa Temple at Ellora, not Mahabalipuram.

 

• Pratihara (Option 2): A North Indian dynasty of the Gurjara-Pratihara empire, unrelated to Mahabalipuram.

 

• Chola (Option 3): Known for the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur, built later than the Mahabalipuram monuments.

question: Which folk music does NOT belong to Nagaland?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nyioga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hereileu, Heliamleu and Neuleu are traditional folk songs/music forms of Nagaland, sung by various Naga tribes on festive and social occasions. (नागालैंड लोक संगीत — न्योगा भिन्न)

 

• Nyioga is not counted among the traditional folk music forms of Nagaland and stands apart from the other three listed here.

 

• Naga folk music is largely oral and community-based, traditionally performed during harvest festivals, tribal gatherings and the Hornbill Festival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nagaland's flagship cultural event, the Hornbill Festival, is held every year from 1 to 10 December at Kisama, near Kohima, and showcases folk music and dance of all major Naga tribes.

 

• Naga folk songs are traditionally sung a cappella in group/choral style, without musical instruments in many traditional forms.

 

NOTE

 

• Hereileu (Option 2): A recognised folk-music form associated with Nagaland.

 

• Heliamleu (Option 3): A recognised folk-music form associated with Nagaland.

 

• Neuleu (Option 4): A recognised folk-music form associated with Nagaland.

question: Article 20 of the Constitution of India is related to _____.
option_1: protection in respect of conviction for offenses
option_3: equality of opportunities in matters of public employment
solution_text:
The correct answer is protection in respect of conviction for offenses.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 20 of the Indian Constitution, under Part III (Fundamental Rights), provides "Protection in respect of conviction for offences". (अनुच्छेद 20 — अपराधों की दोषसिद्धि से संरक्षण)

 

• It guarantees three protections: no ex-post-facto law (no conviction except for violation of a law in force at the time of the act), no double jeopardy (no person prosecuted/punished more than once for the same offence), and no self-incrimination (no person compelled to be a witness against himself).

 

• These protections apply to both citizens and non-citizens and cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21 guarantees the "Protection of life and personal liberty", while Article 22 deals with protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.

 

• Article 20's guarantees are part of the right to life and personal liberty framework and are considered among the most important criminal-law safeguards in the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Abolition of titles (Option 2): Dealt with under Article 18, not Article 20.

 

• Equality of opportunity in public employment (Option 3): Dealt with under Article 16, not Article 20.

 

• Freedom to manage religious affairs (Option 4): Dealt with under Article 26, not Article 20.

question: Which of the following is NOT a poverty alleviation programme in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtriya Ucchatar Shiksha Abhiyan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rashtriya Ucchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), launched in 2013, is a centrally sponsored scheme for improving higher education, not a poverty alleviation programme. (राष्ट्रीय उच्चतर शिक्षा अभियान — उच्च शिक्षा योजना)

 

• RUSA aims to provide strategic funding to eligible state higher educational institutions to improve access, equity and quality in higher education.

 

• Unlike the other three options, RUSA does not target poverty or employment generation among the poor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched in 1997 to provide urban employment to the urban poor.

 

• Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP), launched in 1978-80, aimed at providing self-employment to rural poor families; Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) (1993) aimed at generating self-employment for educated unemployed youth.

 

NOTE

 

• Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (Option 1): A genuine urban poverty-alleviation/employment programme.

 

• Integrated Rural Development Program (Option 3): A genuine rural poverty-alleviation programme.

 

• Prime Minister Rozgar Yojana (Option 4): A genuine self-employment/poverty-alleviation scheme for educated youth.

question: On what type of data can MS Excel functions operate?
option_2: Range of cells or groups of cells
solution_text:
The correct answer is Range of cells or groups of cells.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• MS Excel functions (e.g., SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT) are designed to operate on a range of cells or groups of cells, in addition to individual cells. (एमएस एक्सेल फंक्शन — सेल रेंज पर संचालन)

 

• A range refers to a selection of two or more cells, such as A1:A10, and functions can take such ranges as arguments to perform calculations across many values at once.

 

• This flexibility (operating on single cells, multiple non-contiguous cells, or full ranges) is what makes Excel functions powerful for data analysis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common Excel functions like SUM(), AVERAGE(), MAX(), MIN(), COUNT() commonly take a range as their argument, e.g., `=SUM(A1:A10)`.

 

• Excel also supports named ranges, which allow a range of cells to be referenced by a custom name in formulas.

 

NOTE

 

• External data sources only (Option 1): Excel functions primarily operate on data within the worksheet, not exclusively on external sources.

 

• Entire worksheets only (Option 3): Functions are not restricted to operating on whole worksheets alone.

 

• Individual cells only (Option 4): Functions can operate on individual cells too, but they are not restricted to individual cells alone — they also work on ranges/groups of cells.

question: Which of the following was NOT a venue for the 66th National School Games 2022-23?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ludhiana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 66th National School Games 2022-23, organised by the School Games Federation of India (SGFI), were held across multiple venues including Delhi, Bhopal and Gwalior. (66वीं राष्ट्रीय स्कूल खेल — दिल्ली, भोपाल, ग्वालियर)

 

• Ludhiana was not among the host cities for the 66th edition of the National School Games.

 

• The Games featured school-level athletes competing across a wide range of disciplines, held at multiple centres across Madhya Pradesh and Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The School Games Federation of India (SGFI) is the apex body governing school-level sports competitions in India.

 

• Madhya Pradesh cities such as Bhopal, Gwalior, Indore and Jabalpur have frequently hosted National School Games and Khelo India Youth Games events in recent years.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi (Option 1): A genuine venue for the 66th National School Games 2022-23.

 

• Gwalior (Option 2): A genuine venue for the 66th National School Games 2022-23.

 

• Bhopal (Option 3): A genuine venue for the 66th National School Games 2022-23.

question: Which of the following groups of places in India has little differences in day and night temperatures?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai and Thiruvananthapuram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chennai and Thiruvananthapuram are coastal cities, and coastal areas experience a moderate/equable climate with only a small diurnal (day-night) temperature range. (तटीय जलवायु — चेन्नई, तिरुवनंतपुरम)

 

• This is because water heats up and cools down more slowly than land, so the sea moderates temperature swings in nearby coastal regions throughout the day and night.

 

• In contrast, inland/continental locations heat up quickly during the day and cool down rapidly at night, leading to a larger diurnal temperature range.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Continentality — the effect of distance from the sea — is a major control of climate; regions far from large water bodies (like deserts) show extreme diurnal and annual temperature ranges.

 

• Jaisalmer, located in the Thar Desert, is a classic example of extreme diurnal temperature variation due to low humidity and lack of moderating water bodies.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhopal and Indore (Option 1): Both are inland plateau cities in Madhya Pradesh with comparatively larger diurnal temperature ranges than coastal cities.

 

• Jammu and Kashmir (Option 3): These are inland/hilly regions with considerable day-night and seasonal temperature variation.

 

• Jaipur and Jaisalmer (Option 4): Both are semi-arid/desert cities of Rajasthan known for large diurnal temperature ranges, not small ones.

question: Which of the following is the festival of Kerala that heralds the harvest season, lasts for 10 days, and has snake boat races etc?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Onam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Onam is the most important harvest festival of Kerala, celebrated over 10 days in the Malayalam month of Chingam (August-September). (ओणम — केरल का फसल उत्सव)

 

• It commemorates the legendary homecoming of King Mahabali and is marked by Pookalam (floral rangoli), the grand Onasadya feast, Kaikottikali dance, and the famous Vallam Kali (snake boat races), particularly the Nehru Trophy Boat Race on the Pamba river.

 

• Onam is celebrated by people of Kerala across religions and is regarded as the state festival of Kerala.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Thiruvathira is a Kerala festival/dance associated with Lord Shiva, mainly celebrated by women.

 

• Vishu marks the Malayalam New Year, while Thrissur Pooram is a famous temple festival held at the Vadakkunnathan Temple, Thrissur, known for its grand elephant processions.

 

NOTE

 

• Thiruvathira (Option 1): A Kerala festival honouring Lord Shiva, not a harvest festival with boat races.

 

• Thrissur Pooram (Option 3): A famous temple festival known for caparisoned elephants, not a harvest festival.

 

• Vishu (Option 4): The Malayalam New Year festival, distinct from Onam.

question: When was the Bharat Nirman Programme launched by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bharat Nirman Programme was launched by the Government of India in 2005 as a time-bound business plan for rural infrastructure development. (भारत निर्माण योजना — 2005)

 

• It focused on six components: irrigation, rural roads, rural housing, rural water supply, rural electrification, and rural telecommunication connectivity.

 

• The programme was implemented in phases, with Bharat Nirman Phase-I (2005-09) and Phase-II (2009-12).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharat Nirman was a flagship programme of the UPA government, complementing schemes like NREGA (2005) and the National Rural Health Mission (2005).

 

• Under Bharat Nirman, targets included connecting all villages with a population above 1,000 (500 in hilly/tribal areas) with all-weather roads.

 

NOTE

 

• 2010 (Option 1): Incorrect; not the launch year of Bharat Nirman.

 

• 2014 (Option 2): Incorrect; this is when the NDA government took office, not the launch year of Bharat Nirman.

 

• 2000 (Option 4): Incorrect; too early — Bharat Nirman was launched in 2005.

question: 'Chhau' is a popular dance of which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance form that combines martial, tribal and folk traditions, performed using elaborate masks, vigorous footwork and mock-combat movements. (छऊ नृत्य — झारखंड)

 

• It has three regional styles named after their home areas: Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

 

• Chhau dance was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhau dance traditionally depicts episodes from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, along with local folklore and nature themes.

 

• Unlike the Purulia and Mayurbhanj styles, Seraikella Chhau dancers perform in masks throughout, and the form is closely associated with the former royal family of Seraikella.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Known for folk dances such as Garba and Dandiya Ras, not Chhau.

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Known for classical/folk forms such as Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, and Theyyam, not Chhau.

 

• Haryana (Option 3): Known for folk dances such as Phag and Dhamal, not Chhau.

question: What is the main objective of Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA), 2003?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To reduce fiscal deficit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 was enacted to ensure inter-generational equity in fiscal management and to institutionalise fiscal discipline. (राजकोषीय उत्तरदायित्व एवं बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम — राजकोषीय घाटा कम करना)

 

• Its principal objective was to reduce the fiscal deficit and revenue deficit of the Government of India and to eliminate revenue deficit over a defined period, bringing down the fiscal deficit to a manageable level.

 

• The Act also mandated greater transparency in fiscal operations through documents such as the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement presented along with the Union Budget.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FRBM Act came into force in 2004, though it was enacted in 2003; it has been amended several times, notably in 2018 based on the N.K. Singh Committee recommendations.

 

• The Act set a target fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP, subject to escape clauses for exceptional circumstances.

 

NOTE

 

• To reduce subsidies (Option 1): A possible tool for fiscal consolidation, but not the Act's stated main objective.

 

• To increase exports (Option 2): Relates to trade policy, not the FRBM Act.

 

• To increase excise duty (Option 4): A taxation matter, not the core objective of the FRBM Act.

question: How do the muscle cells help in movement?
option_1: The lining of the vessels inside help in movement.
option_2: The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.
option_3: The blood flow of the cells helps in movement.
option_4: The thickness of the cell layer helps in movement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muscle cells (myocytes) contain specialised contractile proteins — actin and myosin — that allow the cell to change shape by contracting and relaxing. (पेशी कोशिकाएँ — संकुचन एवं शिथिलन)

 

• This contraction and relaxation of muscle fibres, when coordinated across many cells, generates the force needed for movement of body parts and organs.

 

• Muscle tissue is broadly classified into skeletal (voluntary), smooth (involuntary), and cardiac muscle, all of which function on this basic principle of contraction-relaxation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Skeletal muscles are attached to bones via tendons and enable voluntary movement of limbs and body parts.

 

• Muscle contraction is triggered by nerve impulses that cause calcium ion release, initiating the sliding filament mechanism between actin and myosin filaments.

 

NOTE

 

• The lining of the vessels inside help in movement (Option 1): Describes blood vessel lining (endothelium), not the mechanism of muscle movement.

 

• The blood flow of the cells helps in movement (Option 3): Blood flow supplies oxygen/nutrients to muscles but is not itself the mechanism producing movement.

 

• The thickness of the cell layer helps in movement (Option 4): Cell layer thickness is not the basis of muscular movement.

question: What will happen when you select the cell contents of a particular row in MS-Excel and then click the Delete button?
option_1: Entries in all the selected cells will be deleted
option_2: Only first three cells will be deleted
option_4: First five cell entries will be deleted
solution_text:
The correct answer is Entries in all the selected cells will be deleted.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Excel, pressing the Delete key after selecting a range of cells removes only the contents (data/values) of those selected cells. (एमएस एक्सेल — डिलीट बटन)

 

• It does not remove the row itself, nor does it affect the cell formatting, and it does not delete any cells outside the selection.

 

• To delete the entire row (including the row structure), one must instead use right-click → Delete → Entire Row, or the "Delete" command in the Cells group of the Home tab → Delete Sheet Rows, not the simple Delete key.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pressing Delete clears content but preserves cell formatting (borders, fonts, colours); to remove formatting too, one uses Clear All (Home → Editing → Clear → Clear All).

 

• The Backspace key, unlike Delete, only clears the content of the active cell, not an entire multi-cell selection.

 

NOTE

 

• Only first three cells will be deleted (Option 2): Incorrect; Delete acts on the entire selected range, not just three cells.

 

• Entire row will be deleted (Option 3): Incorrect; the Delete key only clears cell contents, it does not remove the row structure.

 

• First five cell entries will be deleted (Option 4): Incorrect; there is no such restriction to five cells.

question: The Reserve Bank of India was fully nationalised and owned by the Government of India in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1949.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), originally established as a private shareholders' bank on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, was nationalised on 1 January 1949. (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक — 1949 में राष्ट्रीयकरण)

 

• After nationalisation, the RBI became wholly owned by the Government of India.

 

• The RBI serves as India's central bank, responsible for monetary policy, currency issuance, and regulation of the banking sector, headquartered in Mumbai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Governor of RBI was Sir Osborne Smith; the first Indian Governor was C.D. Deshmukh.

 

• RBI's Central Board of Directors is currently headed by a Governor appointed by the Government of India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1950 (Option 2): Incorrect; India adopted its Constitution in 1950, unrelated to RBI nationalisation.

 

• 1947 (Option 3): Incorrect; this is India's year of independence, not RBI's nationalisation year.

 

• 1948 (Option 4): Incorrect; RBI's nationalisation took effect from 1 January 1949, not 1948.

question: Orographic rainfall occurs when _____________.
option_2: the air masses collide at Intertropical Conversion Zone
option_3: saturated air mass comes across a mountain
option_4: hot air rises up in conventional currents
solution_text:
The correct answer is saturated air mass comes across a mountain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Orographic rainfall (relief rainfall) occurs when a moisture-laden (saturated) air mass is forced to rise over a mountain barrier. (पर्वतीय (उच्चावच) वर्षा — नमी युक्त वायु का पर्वत से टकराना)

 

• As the air rises, it cools adiabatically, reaching its dew point, causing water vapour to condense and fall as rain on the windward slope of the mountain.

 

• The leeward slope, having lost most of its moisture, receives little rainfall and often becomes a rain shadow area.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Example: The Western Ghats receive heavy orographic rainfall on their western (windward) slopes from the south-west monsoon, while the eastern (leeward) side remains comparatively dry.

 

• Other types of rainfall include convectional rainfall (from rising hot air) and cyclonic/frontal rainfall (from air-mass convergence).

 

NOTE

 

• A cyclone makes a landfall (Option 1): Describes cyclonic rainfall, not orographic rainfall.

 

• Air masses collide at ITCZ (Option 2): Describes convergence/convectional rainfall near the Intertropical Convergence Zone, not orographic rainfall.

 

• Hot air rises in convection currents (Option 4): Describes convectional rainfall, not orographic rainfall.

question: The fifth edition of the Khelo India Youth Games were organised in Bhopal city in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 5th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2023 was hosted by Madhya Pradesh, with Bhopal as one of the principal host venues. (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स 2023 — भोपाल, मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• KIYG 2023 was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and featured athletes competing across numerous disciplines.

 

• Khelo India Youth Games is a national-level multi-sport event, launched in 2018, aimed at promoting sports culture among school and college-going youth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1st edition of KIYG was held in New Delhi (2018); subsequent editions were held in Pune (2019), Guwahati (2020), and Panchkula/Haryana (2021, held in 2022).

 

• Madhya Pradesh has emerged as a frequent host of major national sporting events in recent years.

 

NOTE

 

• 2022 (Option 1): Incorrect; not the year of the 5th edition in Bhopal.

 

• 2020 (Option 2): Incorrect; the 2020 edition (3rd) was held in Guwahati, Assam.

 

• 2021 (Option 3): Incorrect; the corresponding edition, delayed to 2022, was held in Haryana.

question: In April 2023, Government of India launched Vibrant Village Programme from Kibithoo village which is located in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vibrant Village Programme (VVP), aimed at comprehensive development of villages along India's northern border, was launched from Kibithoo village, located in the Anjaw district of Arunachal Pradesh, in April 2023. (वाइब्रेंट विलेज प्रोग्राम — किबिथू, अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• Kibithoo is one of the easternmost inhabited villages of India, situated close to the India-China (Line of Actual Control) border.

 

• The programme focuses on developing infrastructure, connectivity, livelihood opportunities and tourism in border villages to check depopulation/migration from border areas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vibrant Village Programme was approved by the Union Cabinet in February 2023 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, covering border villages of Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Ladakh.

 

• The scheme complements the government's broader "Border Area Development Programme (BADP)".

 

NOTE

 

• Meghalaya (Option 1): Not the location of Kibithoo village.

 

• Bihar (Option 2): An inland state with no international northern border; not the location of Kibithoo.

 

• Assam (Option 4): A northeastern state, but Kibithoo lies in Arunachal Pradesh, not Assam.

question: In July 2021, which state government passed a resolution supporting an ad hoc committee report that favoured the creation of a legislative council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 2021, the West Bengal Legislative Assembly passed a resolution supporting the report of an ad hoc committee favouring the creation of a Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council) for the state. (पश्चिम बंगाल विधान परिषद — जुलाई 2021)

 

• A Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper house of a state legislature, created or abolished under Article 169 of the Constitution, requiring a resolution passed by the state's Legislative Assembly followed by a Parliament Act.

 

• West Bengal previously had a Legislative Council which was abolished in 1969; this resolution was a step towards its re-creation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• As of the time of this exam, only a few Indian states — Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh — have a bicameral legislature with a Legislative Council.

 

• Under Article 169, Parliament may create or abolish a Legislative Council in a state if the State's Legislative Assembly passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 2): Already has an existing Legislative Council; not the state that passed this particular 2021 resolution.

 

• Telangana (Option 3): Already has an existing Legislative Council; not the state referred to here.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): Does not have a Legislative Council and was not the state that passed this 2021 resolution.
